extraction.name: PIQA: Physical Interaction: Question Answering
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning in natural language, framed as a two-choice question answering task where a model or human is given a goal and must choose the correct physical solution between a valid solution and an incorrect trick solution.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi
extraction.publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was gathered using prompts derived from instructables.com across six categories (costume, outside, craft, home, food, and workshop). Annotators reviewed instructions to construct two component tasks, articulating a physical goal, a valid solution, and an invalid solution (a trick). Data was collected in batches of several thousand triples and validated by other annotators.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: User-generated content data, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Examples were tokenized using Spacy and the GPT BPE tokenizer. The dataset was cleaned of stylistic artifacts and trivial examples using the AFLite algorithm, which fine-tuned BERT-Large on 5,000 examples and used an ensemble of linear classifiers on pre-computed embeddings to filter out biased instances and split data into train, development, and test sets. Examples were truncated at 150 tokens.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdsourced annotators were asked to provide a physical goal, a valid solution, and an invalid trick solution that sounds reasonable but fails due to subtle physical or precondition misunderstandings. Annotators were required to pass a qualification HIT (>80% accuracy) identifying well-formed pairs before participating, and their work was validated by other annotators.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (implied via HITs and turkerview.com)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed from the data, which often filtered out instances requiring expert-level domain knowledge. Workers with low agreement were disqualified. Human performance was calculated via majority vote among qualified annotators.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes reporting bias in text where commonsense properties and everyday physical facts are rarely directly reported, and annotators initially defaulted to prototypical solutions (e.g., kitchen or garage tools). Systematic annotation artifacts and data biases were mitigated using the AFLite algorithm.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Some development errors identified as mistakes were actually correct but required a web search to verify. Examples requiring expert-level domain knowledge rather than general commonsense were removed.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking, training, validation, and testing of natural language understanding models on physical commonsense reasoning.
